7.blurb: The Khitan Liao who show up in Chapter 7 as the dynasty Yelü Dashi was fleeing are the same empire that invaded Korea three times between 993 and 1019. This is the Goryeo side of that collision: Korea under siege from the same horse-people whose later collapse would send a fragment of their ruling class fleeing west across the continent to found the Qara-Khitai.

The Jurchen Jin who destroyed the Liao and sent Yelü Dashi fleeing west were the same dynasty that would turn on Song China and capture the northern capital in 1127, forcing the Song to reestablish as the Southern Song. This chapter covers that catastrophe from the Chinese side: the loss of the north, the scramble south, and the commercial revolution that let the truncated Song thrive anyway.

While the Qara-Khitai ruled Central Asia with deliberate tolerance — a Buddhist dynasty that taxed its Muslim subjects but never policed their faith — the Almohads were the mirror image at the far end of the Dar al-Islam: a Berber reform movement (al-Muwahhidun, 'the Unitarians') that swept al-Andalus and the Maghreb imposing a severe, doctrinaire orthodoxy and narrowing the philosophical openness earlier Andalusi rulers had tolerated. This chapter is that Almohad order in Spain.
